module.label: Order History
module.title: Order Management
module.summary: Find and manage existing corporate orders, including lifecycle status, order details, fulfilment data, device assignment, eSIM activation and customer transactions.

flows.title: Open Order History and load latest orders
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in active OrdersPage implementation
flows.trigger: Select Order History or navigate to /admin/orders.
flows.summary: Load the latest open and pending orders within the operator's partner, group and source scope.
preconditions: The operator is authenticated and authorized to view Order History.
The login state contains user_id, group_id and source.
The order service can enforce the same corporate scope sent by the client.
flows.outcome: The table contains the latest scoped orders, or a distinct empty/error state is shown.

steps.title: Open Order History
steps.detail: The /admin/orders route renders OrdersPage and the Order Management interface.

steps.title: Build scoped request
steps.detail: Use the logged-in user as partner_id and include group_id, source and order_date selection.

steps.title: Request latest orders
steps.detail: Search the recent date window for order statuses Open (0) and Pending (8).

steps.title: Request successful?
steps.detail: On success replace the View list; on failure retain an explicit error rather than treating it as an empty result.

steps.title: Render order table
steps.detail: Show the returned orders with status, dates, plan, product and available actions.

branches.label: Orders returned
branches.detail: Render only the backend-authorized result.

branches.label: Valid empty result
branches.detail: Show No orders found for the current latest-order criteria.

branches.label: Technical failure
branches.detail: Show an error and Retry without replacing the failure with an empty table.

branches.label: Unauthorized
branches.detail: Deny the route and do not expose order data.

apis.name: getLatestOrders
apis.purpose: Load recent open and pending orders for the authenticated corporate scope.

rules.text: Order results must be restricted to the authenticated operator's authorized partner, group and source scope.
The default latest list includes only Open and Pending orders in the configured recent date window.
Backend authorization must not rely on partner_id supplied by the browser alone.

gaps.text: Fetch failures are logged to the console but no visible error or Retry state is set in OrdersPage.
Route-level and action-level permission checks are not demonstrated in the reviewed Order History components.

acceptance.text: Only orders in the operator's authorized scope are returned and displayed.
Loading, empty, failure and unauthorized states are visually distinct.
A failed latest-order request can be retried without reloading the portal.
Unauthorized operators cannot retrieve orders by changing client request fields.

flows.title: Search and filter order history
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in OrdersPage and OrderFilters
flows.trigger: Choose status, date range and sort field, then select Search.
flows.summary: Search existing orders by lifecycle status and date window while preserving corporate scope.
preconditions: Order History is open.
The operator has permission to search orders.
Start date, end date and status form a valid search request.
flows.outcome: The View list is replaced by orders matching the submitted filters.

steps.title: Choose filters
steps.detail: Select order status, start date, end date and order-date or travel-start sorting.

steps.title: Apply source rules
steps.detail: ChargeGo hides unsupported lifecycle statuses and defaults to All; other sources default to Open.

steps.title: Build search request
steps.detail: Merge filters into the scoped base request and convert order_status to a number.

steps.title: Search orders
steps.detail: POST getOrders2 for the active View mode.

steps.title: Result successful?
steps.detail: Replace the list on success; otherwise clear or retain data according to a defined failure policy.

steps.title: Show filtered result
steps.detail: Mark the page searched and render the matching orders.

branches.label: All statuses
branches.detail: Use status 10 as the backend sentinel for all supported order states.

branches.label: ChargeGo source
branches.detail: Hide lifecycle states that ChargeGo fulfilment never reaches.

branches.label: No matches
branches.detail: Show a valid empty result without reporting a technical error.

branches.label: Search failure
branches.detail: Preserve the submitted filters and provide Retry.

apis.name: getOrders
apis.purpose: Search scoped orders by lifecycle status and date range.

rules.text: Start date must not be after end date.
Source-specific status options must match lifecycle states supported by the backend.
Every search must retain partner, group and source scope regardless of UI filters.

gaps.text: User and Promo search branches exist in OrdersPage, but their tabs are commented out in the active order-management-ui, so those flows are currently unreachable.
The UI does not visibly validate start date against end date before sending the request.

acceptance.text: Invalid date ranges are blocked with field-level guidance.
The result matches status, dates, sort field and authorized corporate scope.
A failed search preserves filters and shows an actionable error.
Hidden source-specific statuses cannot be submitted by manipulating the browser.

flows.title: Explore, sort, paginate and export orders
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in order-management-ui table configuration
flows.trigger: Use table search, sorting, pagination or CSV export after orders load.
flows.summary: Explore the loaded authorized result and export the current order dataset with spreadsheet-safe columns.
preconditions: An order result has completed loading.
The operator may view the result.
CSV export additionally requires an approved export permission.
flows.outcome: The visible rows or downloaded CSV reflect the authorized order result.

steps.title: Choose a table operation
steps.detail: Search within loaded orders, sort supported columns, change page or request CSV export.

steps.title: Transform loaded rows
steps.detail: SupportTableAdapter applies table search, sorting and pagination to the current result.

steps.title: Export requested?
steps.detail: Use the dedicated csvColumns list rather than rendering action buttons or JSX values.

steps.title: Prepare file
steps.detail: Export identifiers, product, dates, type, charges, plan code and platform.

steps.title: Update or download
steps.detail: Render the table result or download support-orders.csv.

branches.label: Client search
branches.detail: Filter only the orders already returned by the scoped server request.

branches.label: CSV export
branches.detail: Exclude action controls and use plain field values.

branches.label: Export denied
branches.detail: Do not prepare or download order data.

rules.text: Table operations and exports may contain only the already-authorized order result.
Export must exclude action controls and fields not approved for offline use.

gaps.text: OrdersPage implements server CSV handlers, but the active UI uses SupportTableAdapter client export and does not call onDownloadCsv.
An independent export permission check is not visible in the active table configuration.

acceptance.text: Search, sort and pagination never introduce orders outside the server-authorized result.
CSV contains the intended plain-value columns and no action UI.
Operators without export permission cannot download order data.
Exported row count and filters are clear to the operator.

flows.title: Inspect complete order details and close eligible orders
flows.trigger: Select an Order ID in the table.
flows.summary: Review customer, order, travel, plan, shipping, variation and assigned-device data; Mask orders can also be closed.
preconditions: An order row is selected.
The row contains the detail, variation and orderDetails data returned by the list API.
Close Order requires lifecycle permission and an eligible Mask order.
flows.outcome: The operator understands the complete order context, or an eligible order is moved to Closed status.

steps.title: Open order
steps.detail: Select the linked Order ID.

steps.title: Render order context
steps.detail: Show customer identity, status, charges, travel, plan, tracking, fulfilment and remarks.

steps.title: Render nested records
steps.detail: Show variation rows and assigned device/SIM/eSIM records when present.

steps.title: Mask order?
steps.detail: Only order_type mask displays Close Order in the active modal.

steps.title: Close eligible order
steps.detail: Confirm the operational close action when policy permits.

steps.title: Patch status
steps.detail: On backend success update the order status to Closed (6) in the visible lists.

branches.label: Standard order
branches.detail: Details are read-only and the operator dismisses the modal.

branches.label: Mask order
branches.detail: Close Order is available and submits status 6.

branches.label: Close failure
branches.detail: Keep the modal open, preserve the original status and show the backend message.

apis.name: closeOrder
apis.purpose: Close an eligible order and move it to lifecycle status 6.

rules.text: Order details must display authoritative backend values without silently substituting data from another order.
Close Order is allowed only for lifecycle states and order types approved by policy.
A close transition must be audited and applied only after backend success.

gaps.text: The modal supports returnTracking, but OrdersPage does not fetch or pass a return tracking value.
The close-order loading and alert props are not wired from OrdersPage, so the modal cannot show reliable progress or result feedback.

acceptance.text: Selecting an Order ID shows details for that exact order.
Variation and device records render only when present and preserve their association with the order.
Close is unavailable for ineligible order types and states.
Close shows progress, success or failure and changes the row only after backend success.

flows.title: Cancel or revert an order
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in confirmation and OrdersPage handlers
flows.trigger: Select the status action for an order row and confirm.
flows.summary: Move Open or Pending orders to Cancelled, or restore a cancelled order to Open, with confirmation and backend-authoritative status.
preconditions: The selected order exists in the operator's authorized scope.
The operator may perform the requested lifecycle transition.
The current order status is authoritative and eligible.
flows.outcome: The order status changes in all visible lists only after backend success.

steps.title: Current status?
steps.detail: Open (0) and Pending (8) show Cancel; the intended revert transition applies to Cancelled (7).

steps.title: Choose action
steps.detail: Select Cancel or Revert on the order row.

steps.title: Request confirmation
steps.detail: Display a modal before changing the order.

steps.title: Submit transition
steps.detail: POST cancelOrder with status 7 for cancel or status 0 for revert.

steps.title: Backend success?
steps.detail: Patch View and User lists only on a successful response.

steps.title: Show final status
steps.detail: Render Cancelled or Open and record the lifecycle event.

branches.label: Cancel confirmed
branches.detail: Set order_status to 7.

branches.label: Revert confirmed
branches.detail: Set order_status to 0.

branches.label: Confirmation dismissed
branches.detail: Send no request and leave the order unchanged.

branches.label: Transition rejected
branches.detail: Keep the authoritative old status and show the backend reason.

apis.name: cancelOrder
apis.purpose: Cancel an order or revert a cancelled order to Open.

rules.text: Only Open and Pending orders may be cancelled through this flow.
Only Cancelled orders may be reverted to Open through this flow.
Lifecycle transitions require confirmation, backend validation and an audit record.

gaps.text: The active UI shows Revert for every status other than Open or Pending, not only Cancelled, so Shipped, Returned and Closed orders can present an invalid transition.
The processing state is never set around cancel/revert calls, so action buttons do not reliably disable or show progress.

acceptance.text: Cancel appears only for Open and Pending orders.
Revert appears only for Cancelled orders.
A pending transition cannot be submitted twice.
Failure preserves the previous status and displays the backend reason.

flows.title: Edit fulfilment data and apply charge controls
flows.actor: Operator with Edit Order or Charge Control permission
flows.trigger: Select Edit for an existing order.
flows.summary: Update tracking, travel dates, remarks, device count and location, or apply separately authorized suppression and charge/refund controls.
preconditions: An order row is selected.
The latest authoritative order record is available.
Financial controls require separate permission from ordinary order editing.
flows.outcome: Approved order fields or charge-control fields are saved and the visible row reflects backend success.

steps.title: Open Edit Order
steps.detail: Load tracking, dates, remarks, device quantity and location from the selected row.

steps.title: Change operational fields
steps.detail: Choose courier/tracking values, travel dates, remarks, device count or order location.

steps.title: Operational or financial update?
steps.detail: Save Order submits orderFields; Apply Suppress / Charges submits a separate chaRef object.

steps.title: Validate permission and fields
steps.detail: Verify dates, quantity, reason, amount, currency and allowed action on the server.

steps.title: Update order
steps.detail: POST updateOrderDetails with order_id and the selected field set.

steps.title: Patch or confirm
steps.detail: Update visible operational fields after success and show an auditable charge-control result.

branches.label: Save operational fields
branches.detail: Patch the View and User rows after backend success.

branches.label: Suppress charges/notifications
branches.detail: Require permission and a reason before applying.

branches.label: Charge or refund
branches.detail: Validate amount, currency and downstream payment result.

branches.label: Validation/API failure
branches.detail: Keep edits, show field-level guidance and do not patch the row.

apis.name: updateOrderDetails
apis.purpose: Update operational fields or authorized charge-control fields for an order.

rules.text: Operational edits and financial controls require distinct permissions and audit events.
End date cannot precede start date and device quantity must be a positive whole number.
Charge suppression, notification suppression, charges and refunds require an explicit reason and backend authorization.

gaps.text: The same modal exposes ordinary order edits and sensitive suppress/charge/refund controls without a visible separate permission boundary.
EditOrderModal initializes local form state only on component creation; selecting a different order later can retain stale values from the first opened order.
Suppress/charge updates do not patch the row or show a wired result state in OrdersPage.

acceptance.text: Each modal opening reflects the currently selected order, never stale local state.
Invalid dates, quantities and financial inputs are blocked before submission.
Financial controls require independent backend permission and a mandatory reason.
Success and failure are visible and the row changes only after backend success.

flows.title: Assign, swap or bulk-assign devices
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in AssignDevice and bulkAssignDeviceFlow
flows.trigger: Select Assign Device(s) for an order.
flows.summary: Assign one device, swap an existing device, or process multiple device IDs from text, ICCID range or XLSX while preventing already-assigned devices.
preconditions: The order is eligible for device assignment.
Device type and required order fulfilment fields are known.
The operator has assignment permission for the order and inventory scope.
flows.outcome: Eligible devices are assigned or swapped, result rows are shown, the order status is recalculated and the visible row is patched.

steps.title: Choose assignment mode
steps.detail: Select Single Device, Swap Device or Multiple Devices.

steps.title: Provide device IDs
steps.detail: Enter one device, old/new swap IDs, up to 30 comma-separated IDs, an ICCID range or an XLSX file.

steps.title: Normalize assignment request
steps.detail: Build the order, customer, device, shipping and flow context; swaps identify both old and new devices.

steps.title: Check assignment
steps.detail: Call isDeviceAssigned before each assign/swap operation.

steps.title: Device available?
steps.detail: Reject already-assigned devices; otherwise call UpdateAssignDevices.

steps.title: Patch order and results
steps.detail: Use the returned recalculated order for single/swap and show per-device bulk results.

branches.label: Single assign
branches.detail: Assign one normalized device ID and log a shipped-device audit action.

branches.label: Swap
branches.detail: Assign the replacement while sending swap_device and suppressing promo re-charge.

branches.label: Bulk
branches.detail: Process text, range or XLSX IDs sequentially and pause after each batch of 50.

branches.label: Already assigned
branches.detail: Do not update the order and return a per-device failure message.

apis.name: isDeviceAssigned
apis.purpose: Prevent assignment of a device that is already in use.

apis.name: UpdateAssignDevices
apis.purpose: Assign or swap a device and return the recalculated order.

rules.text: A device must pass availability, type, inventory-scope and order-eligibility checks before assignment.
A swap must identify the current and replacement device and must not apply the original promo twice.
Every assignment and swap requires an audit trail tied to the acting operator.

gaps.text: The assignment request includes fallback token_id 1234 and card_id 123 when authoritative payment context is unavailable.
Bulk assignment deliberately skips one audit-history call per device, so its audit completeness depends on backend logging not shown here.
Bulk result completion and validation paths are complex and do not visibly provide a safe resume mechanism after interruption.

acceptance.text: An already-assigned, incompatible or out-of-scope device cannot be assigned.
Swap records both device IDs and updates the order exactly once.
Bulk input validates count, headers, identifiers and per-device results before reporting completion.
Every successful single, swap and bulk assignment is attributable to the acting operator.

flows.title: Activate an eligible eSIM order
flows.evidence: AS-IS traced in active table action and API dispatcher
flows.trigger: Select Activate on an Open buy-eSIM order and confirm.
flows.summary: Activate an eligible eSIM for the selected order using its source and customer identifiers.
preconditions: The order status is Open (0).
The order type is buyesim/buy-esim or device_type is E.
The order contains order_id, user_id, app_user_id and request_source.
flows.outcome: The backend activates the eSIM and the order presents a visible terminal result.

steps.title: Evaluate eligibility
steps.detail: Show Activate only for Open eSIM orders.

steps.title: Request activation
steps.detail: Select Activate beside the Order ID.

steps.title: Confirm action
steps.detail: Require confirmation before sending the request.

steps.title: Activate eSIM
steps.detail: Dispatch orderId, source, userId, appUserId and platform crm.

steps.title: Activation successful?
steps.detail: Show success and refresh/patch state; otherwise show the backend reason and allow safe retry.

branches.label: Eligible
branches.detail: Confirm and submit the activation request.

branches.label: Ineligible
branches.detail: Do not render the Activate action.

branches.label: Activation failure
branches.detail: Keep the current order state and show an actionable error.

apis.name: activateEsim
apis.purpose: Activate the eSIM associated with an eligible order.

rules.text: Activate is available only for an Open order positively identified as eSIM.
Activation must be idempotent and audited against order, customer and operator.
A successful activation must update or refresh the visible order state.

gaps.text: OrdersPage awaits activateEsim but ignores the response and does not patch the order, refresh the list or show success/failure.
The processing state is not set during activation, so repeat clicks are not reliably blocked.

acceptance.text: Activate appears only for eligible Open eSIM orders.
A pending activation cannot be submitted twice.
Success or failure is visible and the row is refreshed or patched from authoritative data.
Retry cannot create a duplicate activation.

flows.title: View transactions for an order customer
flows.trigger: Select Transactions beside a User ID when the portal source allows it.
flows.summary: Load and display the selected order customer's transaction history with source normalization.
preconditions: The selected order contains user_id and app_user_id.
The active portal source is not urwifi under the current visibility rule.
The operator may view the customer's financial transaction data.
flows.outcome: The modal shows the customer's transaction rows or a clear empty/error state.

steps.title: Transactions visible?
steps.detail: The active UI shows the action when source is not urwifi and the view is not hidden.

steps.title: Open transactions
steps.detail: Select the transaction action beside the customer User ID.

steps.title: Normalize source
steps.detail: Use a supported request_source value or fall back to urwifi.

steps.title: Request transactions
steps.detail: Dispatch userId, appUserId and source to getUserTrans.

steps.title: Render transaction table
steps.detail: Show email, order, product, charge, currency, type, date and amount.

branches.label: Transactions returned
branches.detail: Render the returned financial records.

branches.label: Valid empty result
branches.detail: Show No transactions found.

branches.label: Technical failure
branches.detail: Show an error and Retry instead of an empty result.

branches.label: Permission denied
branches.detail: Do not display the action or expose transaction data.

apis.name: getUserTrans
apis.purpose: Load transaction history for the selected order customer.

rules.text: Transaction visibility requires explicit financial-data permission, not only a source-name check.
The requested customer must belong to the selected authorized order.
Transaction failure must not be represented as a valid empty history.

gaps.text: The visible transaction authorization rule is source !== urwifi rather than a demonstrated role or permission check.
Transaction API failures are logged but the modal receives an empty list, making failure indistinguishable from no transactions.
A deposit-refund handler exists in OrdersPage, but its active table column is commented out, leaving that workflow dormant and undocumented as an available action.

acceptance.text: Only an operator with transaction-view permission can open or retrieve the data.
The request customer is verified against the selected order and authorized corporate scope.
Loading, empty and failure states are distinct in the modal.
Sensitive transaction fields are limited to those required for support operations.
